title: Research note: The spread of political misinformation on online subcultural platforms
screen_reason: Content/link analysis of the external websites shared on 4chan's /pol/ board (US-flagged posters) and a curated set of US-politics subreddits between 11 Jan 2019 and 25 Mar 2020. Hostnames above a mention threshold were hand-coded into news versus 'junk' (conspiracy, propaganda, sensationalism), and the paper reports the share of shared websites that is junk on each platform (about one third on 4chan, almost 20% on Reddit) plus the propaganda subcategory on 4chan (22%). 'Junk news' is explicitly in scope for this review.

estimates.country: United States (4chan /pol/ posts from users automatically flagged as posting from a US IP address)
estimates.measure_type: % of the websites shared on 4chan /pol/ that were coded as 'junk' (conspiracy, propaganda or sensationalism)
estimates.value_raw: "on 4chan 'junk' information makes up over a third of sources shared"; Finding 2 header: "'Junk' information makes up 1/3 of information sources on 4chan"; Finding 1: "(some one-third overall)"
estimates.denominator: 182 hostnames shared on 4chan /pol/ with more than 400 mentions over the period, hand-coded by the research team
estimates.definition: website coded as conspiracy ('patently untrue or historically conspiratorial narratives'), propaganda ('websites that misrepresent facts for political ends') or sensationalism ('factual websites that nevertheless emphasize salacious or clickbait perspectives'); the three together are called 'junk'
estimates.misinfo_def: "we define 'junk' information as that which masquerades as news, but isn't created to serve as journalistic content. Instead, it focuses on garnering clicks through sensationalist claims; pushing an ideological agenda through propaganda; or spreading conspiracies to sow distrust in mainstream information sources"
estimates.source_quote:
On
Reddit, almost 20% of all shared websites are classified as such, while on 4chan “junk” information makes
up over a third of sources shared.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: "This hostname list was manually coded by a team of researchers, using qualitative observation of the front page of each website's content." No inter-coder reliability, no external list; coding definitions given in a methodological appendix. Only hostnames above a mention threshold were coded.
estimates.moderator_quote:
In order to create similarly sized sample sets, we only coded websites with more than 2,000 mentions
on Reddit and 400 on 4chan. This yielded 203 results from Reddit and 182 from 4chan.
estimates.notes: JUDGEMENT CALLS for an adjudicator. (1) CONSTRUCT: the denominator is the set of websites users shared in these forums, and the paper's framing is 'the spread of political misinformation', so this is SHARING/content_share rather than CONTENT; note the unit is distinct hostnames, not individual share events, so it is unweighted by how often each site was posted. (2) QUALITY CONTAMINATION: the 'junk' aggregate includes a sensationalism category defined as 'factual websites that nevertheless emphasize salacious or clickbait perspectives' - a wholly true item can carry that label, which under the QUALITY-vs-CONTENT rule would push the aggregate towards QUALITY; hence borderline=true. The propaganda-only row below is the truth-based subset. (3) VALUE PRECISION: the paper never prints an exact 4chan figure, only 'over a third' / 'some one-third overall' / '1/3'; 33.3 is the reading of that. (4) breadth left blank because the classification is at source level. (5) year: the collection window spans Jan 2019 - Mar 2020; 2019 is recorded as the representative year (the window's midpoint is ~Aug 2019).

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same manual hostname coding by the research team from the websites' front pages; subreddit list derived from the crowd-sourced 'userleansbot' list, narrowed to subreddits exclusively or primarily about American national politics; posts scraped via the Pushshift Reddit API.
estimates.moderator_quote:
We
examined the list of subreddits that userleansbot relies on and how the bot codes them for partisanship,
and then narrowed our criteria to subreddits that were either exclusively or primarily concerned with
American national politics.
estimates.notes: Value is 'almost 20%' (the finding header rounds it to 1/5), so 20 is a slight overstatement of the paper's wording. Same QUALITY-contamination caveat as the 4chan row (the junk aggregate includes factual-but-sensationalist sites). COUNTRY: only the subreddits' subject matter is American; unlike the 4chan sample there is no user-level geolocation, so 'United States' is a topical rather than a user-population attribution.

estimates.moderator_quote:
News websites were those that adhere to journalistic norms, while
our “junk” content was broken down into conspiracy (patently untrue or historically conspiratorial
narratives); propaganda (websites that misrepresent facts for political ends); and sensationalism (factual
websites that nevertheless emphasize salacious or “clickbait” perspectives).
estimates.notes: Narrower, truth-based definition of the same 4chan cell (propaganda only, excluding sensationalism and conspiracy), hence definition_variant=true. This is the subcategory an adjudicator should prefer if the junk aggregate is judged too quality-contaminated to pool. The conspiracy and sensationalism subcategory shares are not printed (the paper only says the two platforms 'differ by at most 3%' on them).

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, with reasons: (a) ZERO FINDING - 'On neither 4chan's /pol/ board nor in the political subreddits did we find any imposter news websites, otherwise known as "pink slime."' This is a genuine null prevalence for a specific misinformation type and is one of the paper's headline claims, but no denominator or percentage is stated (the pink-slime hostname list was queried against the full post populations), so no row was created. An adjudicator wanting to record it would need a 0% row with the coded-hostname denominators. (b) 'a little over 60% of all sources being categorized as [news]' - a share of legitimate news, not of misinformation. (c) 'approximately two-thirds of the shared news sites are considered mostly neutral in their factual accuracy and reporting' - the hyperpartisan share would be a complement I would have to compute (R8), and the base is news sites only. (d) 'on 4chan's /pol/, nearly 15% have since been removed' - the share of linked YouTube videos later deleted by YouTube; deletion is a platform-moderation proxy, not a misinformation classification, and the Reddit counterpart is given only as 'much lower'. (e) Platform-composition figures (YouTube 41% of 4chan links, ~10% of Reddit links; YouTube shared 9.15x Twitter; BitChute 6th with 28,827 links) - not misinformation shares. (f) Alternative Influence Network popularity comparisons - counts and rankings in Figure 4, no denominators. (g) Post counts in footnote 3 (25,872,606 US-flag posts; 4,173,476 excluded custom-flag posts) describe the frame, not a numerator.

rob.design: Cross-platform link analysis, 11 Jan 2019 - 25 Mar 2020. 4chan: all /pol/ posts containing URLs from users auto-flagged with a US flag (posts from custom flags, 4,173,476, excluded; 25,872,606 US-flag posts in the period), captured with 4CAT. Reddit: posts scraped from the Pushshift API for a curated list of political subreddits derived from the crowd-sourced 'userleansbot' list and narrowed to US national politics. Hostnames were counted and only those above a mention threshold (>2,000 Reddit, >400 4chan) were coded, yielding 203 and 182 hostnames - a rank-truncated, unweighted denominator. Coding was manual, by a team of researchers, from qualitative observation of each site's front page; no inter-coder reliability, no external reliability list, and one of the three junk subcategories (sensationalism) is explicitly compatible with factually accurate sites. YouTube video metadata collected separately via the DMI YouTube data tools. A research note (HKS Misinformation Review), so reporting is brief and several figures appear only in charts.
